SMTO-LLM-0009 — Model stream was malformed

GUID: 8e692070-74b2-4f10-84fe-d918f82d5ea0
Slug: llm-stream-malformed-event
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • Part of the model's reply arrived in a form SMTO couldn't read, so SMTO stopped that reply. Nothing from it was carried out, and steps the task already finished are unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. If the test also fails, the problem is with the model server, not with your task.
  2. If the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). A one-time glitch clears on a fresh reply, and SMTO did not act on the broken one.
  3. If it happens again, ask the person who manages the model server whether a proxy, load balancer or firewall sits between SMTO and the model. Something that changes or cuts up the reply on its way to SMTO can produce pieces SMTO can't read.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and the model's reply appears without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server, and tell them which model and Endpoint you use. The details leave out the broken piece itself for privacy, so they will need to test the server directly.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The SSE decoder received a data event whose payload was not a single valid JSON object, so the model stream was rejected (llm_stream_malformed_event).

What this means

  • The stream decoder expected a JSON object in a data event but could not decode one. The event contents are intentionally excluded from diagnostics. A provider or proxy formatting defect is possible; this is not a request-size or credential diagnosis.

Why this can happen

  • The data event was invalid JSON, excessively nested, or not an object.

How to diagnose it

  • Have the provider operator compare the event framing with the supported streaming format using a sanitized test. Check whether a proxy is substituting an HTML or text error response.

How to fix it

  • Reproduce with a small streaming request to the configured endpoint's /chat/completions and confirm every data: event carries exactly one JSON object; look for a proxy or load balancer injecting HTML, splitting events or altering SSE framing. Fix the provider or proxy, then resume; the rejected decision authorized no tool call and earlier receipts are unaffected.
  • Ask the provider operator to check the stream format and byte limits with a small test request. Preserve prior tool receipts; do not replay completed operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A controlled stream produces parseable JSON data objects.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The bounded stream decoder rejects the current response; it does not rewrite earlier tool receipts.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
